title: Can we add four sevenths and six sevenths on a number line?
description: Four sevenths and six sevenths are added by hopping along a number line cut into sevenths. The hops land on ten sevenths, the same answer as counting units. Keeko doubts the answer by counting the mark he stands on as a hop.
teaching_notes: One idea: adding on a number line means hopping the second fraction in unit gaps from the first fraction. Watch for students who count the starting mark as a hop.

source: Try adding 4/7 + 6/7 using a number line. Do you get the sam
video_script.why: A learner adds fractions with the same fractional unit on a number line, and sees that the hops agree with counting units.
video_script.substitution: the book's own sum four sevenths plus six sevenths on a number line
video_script.anchor: a number line from zero to two, with each unit cut into seven equal gaps
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts the mark he starts on as the first hop, so he makes only five hops and lands on nine sevenths, one gap too soon.
video_script.payoff_line: the hops land on ten sevenths

final_answer.spoken: yes, the hops land on ten sevenths, which is one and three sevenths, the same answer as before

video_script.fraction_reading: four sevenths, six sevenths, seven sevenths, ten sevenths, three sevenths, nine sevenths
never_show: nine sevenths as a landing mark before Keeko's doubt
maths_rules: mark 0, 1 and 2 and cut each unit into 7 equal gaps; each gap is 1/7
start at 4/7 and hop 6 gaps of 1/7 to the right
the hops pass 7/7 = 1 and land on 10/7
slip: Keeko counts the starting mark as hop 1, makes only 5 hops and lands on 9/7
video_script.design: A number line from zero to two with sevenths stays on the board. Six arcs of one gap each start at four sevenths, pass one, and end at ten sevenths.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a number line from 0 to 2 with each unit cut into 7 equal gaps; the sum 4/7 + 6/7 is written above it; the words same answer? appear

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.line: a number line from zero to two appears, with each unit cut into seven equal gaps
marks.ask: the sum 4/7 + 6/7 is written above the line and the words same answer? appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is from your book, where we add four sevenths and six sevenths on a number line.
<bookmark mark='line'/>We found this sum before, by counting units.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Do we get the same answer on the number line?

beats.on_screen: the number line holds still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the number line from 0 to 2; one gap between two neighbouring marks lights up and is labelled 1/7; an arc of one gap sits above it

marks.gap: one gap between two neighbouring marks lights up and is labelled 1/7
marks.hop: an arc of one gap is drawn above it and labelled one hop

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>On this number line, the gap between two neighbouring marks is one fractional unit, one seventh.
<bookmark mark='hop'/>To add one seventh, we make one hop of one gap to the right.

beats.on_screen: Given: the sum 4/7 + 6/7 on a number line
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the sum is four sevenths plus six sevenths.

beats.on_screen: To find: where the hops land, and whether the answer is the same as before
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find where the hops land, and check the answer.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: mark 0, 1 and 2; cut each unit into 7 equal steps of 1/7

marks.cut: each unit is cut into seven equal steps of 1/7

narration: <bookmark mark='marks'/>Step one, mark zero, one and two on the line.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>Cut each unit into seven equal steps, so that each step is one seventh.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: start at 4/7; hop 6 gaps of 1/7 to the right

marks.hops: six arcs, one gap each, are drawn to the right of the dot and counted 1 to 6

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>Step two, start at four sevenths.
<bookmark mark='hops'/>Hop six gaps of one seventh to the right, and count each hop as we cross a gap.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the hops pass 1 = 7/7 and land on 10/7

marks.pass: the hops cross the mark 1, which is 7/7
marks.land: the last hop ends on the mark 10/7

narration: <bookmark mark='pass'/>Step three, the hops pass the mark one, which is seven sevenths.
<bookmark mark='land'/>The last hop lands on the tenth step of one seventh. That is ten sevenths.

marks.split: the landing mark is split into the first 7 steps up to 1 and 3 more steps

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step four, seven sevenths take us to one, and three more sevenths are left over. That puts us at one whole and three sevenths.

beats.on_screen: Answer: yes; 10/7 = 1 3/7, the same as before

marks.ans: 10/7 = 1 3/7 is written and glows beside the earlier answer

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Yes, the hops land on ten sevenths, which is one and three sevenths, the same answer as before.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says the mark I stand on is hop one: 9/7; the arcs start on the 4/7 mark itself and stop one gap short; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.short: the arcs start on the 4/7 mark itself and stop one gap short of the landing mark

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we land on nine sevenths, because the mark we stand on is hop one.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Standing on a mark is not a hop, so this count stops one gap too soon.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A hop is the gap between two marks. We count the gaps we cross, never the marks we touch.
